clue.text: English trait-fairness

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic or quality

explanation.surface: A claim that fair play is the defining English characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness means treating everyone the same, giving all an even and identical standing.

clue.text: Obscure film extracts in middle of reel

indicators.note: in puts the film extracts inside the central letters
middle of takes the central letters of the word reel

parts.note: clips are short extracts from a film

explanation.surface: Unknown film excerpts shown in the middle of a reel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's film reel fits 'film extracts', but the reel only lends its central pair EE, via 'middle of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to obscure, as the moon blocks out the sun.

clue.text: Jack may be in a predicament

definitions.meaning: a Union Jack flag is hoisted up a flagpole
British slang for being in trouble or muddled

explanation.definitionFit: A flag such as the Union Jack is raised on a flagstaff; the phrase is also British slang for being in difficulty.

clue.text: Hat on, and cape

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America, is often just the Horn

explanation.surface: Putting on a hat and a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leghorn is a straw hat made from plaited Italian wheat straw.

clue.text: Measure concentration of acid turning up in game

indicators.note: in places the turned acid piece inside the game

parts.note: a tie is a game, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tart means sour or acid

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction: test how strong an acid is in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'acid' chemical, but here it simply means sour; 'turning up' in this down clue makes TRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titration is the lab technique for finding the strength of a solution.

clue.text: Extremely protective of Italian girl

indicators.note: being protective of something means wrapping round it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: extremely means very
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone is fiercely overprotective of an Italian girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Rescheduled at ten — live broadcast

indicators.note: rescheduled means rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A live broadcast has been moved to ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is a verb here: to air an opinion publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate an issue is to air it publicly, making it widely known.

clue.text: Kid needs to produce two pounds for cuddly toy

parts.note: to kid is to tease, as is to rag
to do is to produce, as in do a drawing
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two give LL

explanation.surface: A child has to find two pounds for a soft toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to tease; 'needs to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a floppy stuffed doll made of cloth, a soft plaything.

clue.text: Taken in by constable, Australian players arrested on stage

indicators.note: taken in by means held within the following words

explanation.surface: An Australian constable arrests a group of actors in the middle of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a scene where actors freeze motionless, as if held in place.

clue.text: Falsifying it in a log — it can result in legal action

indicators.note: falsifying a record means doctoring it, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctoring an official log is the kind of thing that ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsifying' rearranges IT IN A LOG IT; 'can result in' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigation is the process of taking a dispute to court, which is what a lawsuit is.

clue.text: Pass the fish

definitions.meaning: to ... is to pass, as time or a person does
a small spiny-finned sea fish common in rock pools

explanation.surface: An instruction at the dinner table to hand over the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by means to move past, and the goby is a small fish family found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Singer holding note after sherry, say, that could put one to sleep

definitions.text: that could put one to sleep

indicators.note: after places the singer piece behind the sherry piece
say tells us to take the word as heard, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: fino is a pale dry sherry

indicators.note: holding means the singer clasps the note inside

parts.note: a baritone is a male singer
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer who could send you to sleep after a glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: FINO sounds like 'fee-no', which is spelt PHENO here; BARITONE 'holding' B gives BARBITONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenobarbitone is a barbiturate sedative, a drug used to induce sleep.

clue.text: State units of width and weight

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A request to give measurements in units of width and weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'units of' covers both pieces: an en is a printing measure, half an em wide.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or declare, an old formal synonym for declaring.

clue.text: Support for Indian lines seen out of the corner of one's eye

definitions.meaning: the feet of a member of the Crow people of North America, which hold him up

definitions.text: lines seen out of the corner of one's eye
definitions.meaning: wrinkles fanning out at the outer corners of the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: The Crow are a Native American people, so a Crow's feet support him; the phrase also names wrinkles near the eyes.

clue.text: Fellow everyone gets to make a fool of

definitions.text: Fellow everyone gets to make a fool of

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
everyone means all
to guy someone is to ridicule or mock them

explanation.surface: Describes the man who is everyone's target for jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and also builds the answer; 'gets to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat or dupe, someone set up to be duped or blamed by others.

clue.text: Diver left inside craft on government test

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for left within the craft

parts.note: craft means cunning, guile
the MOT is the British annual roadworthiness test, originally from the Ministry of Transport

explanation.surface: A diver is tested before being allowed onto a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly British vehicle safety test; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Smoke with lady-love in bed

indicators.note: in places the lady-love inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Hero was the beloved of Leander in Greek legend

explanation.surface: Someone smoking in bed alongside their sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady-love' looks like two pieces (HER + O) but HERO, Leander's beloved, is needed: C(HERO)OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something one smokes.

clue.text: Crazy old-fashioned measure supported by Telegraph

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a hay is an old country dance, and measure is an old word for a dance
a wire is a telegram, so to wire is to telegraph

explanation.surface: Something mad about an old unit printed in the Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the British newspaper but is the verb, to send a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means becoming erratic or out of control, wildly unhinged.

clue.text: Red rose represented in church hanging

indicators.note: represented means re-presented, so the letters are given in a new form

explanation.surface: A red rose pictured on a church tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or hanging behind a church altar.

clue.text: Male has row on motorway what's up with the mini?

indicators.note: on puts the row after the motorway

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
M stands for motorway, as in the M1
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A man has an argument on the motorway about his small car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mini' is the miniskirt, not the British small car, and 'row' is a line, not a quarrel; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniskirt's lower edge sits high on the leg, so its edge is literally raised.

clue.text: Athlete — thrower securing first in discus

indicators.note: securing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: a hurler is one who throws

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of discus

explanation.surface: A field athlete clutching a discus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrower' suggests the discus event, but the athlete is one who jumps hurdles.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler runs races over barriers, a track sportsman.

clue.text: Daughter at home in Paris or American capital

indicators.note: at means placed within, so the daughter sits inside the home

parts.note: maison is French for house

explanation.surface: A daughter lives either in Paris or in an American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Madison is the state capital of Wisconsin; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Madison is the seat of government of Wisconsin, a US state.

clue.text: Leader of church gripped by sectarian spirit

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ancient Jewish sect

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of church

explanation.surface: A church leader held by a fanatical sectarian spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect at the time of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence is the vital core or spirit of something.

clue.text: Dray horses like running free in North country area

indicators.note: horses running free move about at random, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brewery dray horses galloping loose through northern countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The YORKSHIRE DALES are upland valleys in northern England, now a national park.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park region of valleys in northern England, part of the north country.

clue.text: Song used misleading words

definitions.meaning: a German art song for voice and piano
told untruths, past tense of fib

explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German romantic song, and lied is the past tense of telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Bull housed in castle

parts.note: John Bull personifies the nation, and the proverb says such a man's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A bull kept inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bull is the stock figure for an English person; the saying is 'an Englishman's home is his castle'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the cartoon personification of a native of England.

clue.text: Manoeuvre carefully during race to get cups, etc.

indicators.note: during places the careful manoeuvre inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
to ease something is to move it gently into place

explanation.surface: Inching forward cautiously in a race to win some trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' suggests trophies for the race winner but means crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of crockery for serving tea: cups, saucers, pot and jug.

clue.text: Dark brown animal caught in trap? On the contrary

indicators.note: caught in places one piece inside the other
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the trap goes inside the animal

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A dark brown creature caught in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes hair of a deep brownish shade.
